m1-fast-start.model_name: Looming threshold -> Mauthner latency -> C-start (yaw) -> CPG burst (M2 thrust, power-capped) -> taxi -> engineering/simulation/glide.py
m1-fast-start.context: 3D point-body Monte Carlo (20,000 draws) over the priors listed in the manifest. Each prior is tagged abstract_verified (PubMed abstract read this session), recalled_not_reread or assumption. It feeds the project's existing organism glide model with a launch-speed distribution in place of its fixed V0 = 12 m/s.
m1-fast-start.time_units: seconds of escape, burst, taxi and glide (physical time of the point-body model)

equations.label: Looming trigger (angular size threshold)
equations.source: Preuss et al. 2006 (threshold on a scaled angular size; values assumed)

equations.label: Burst speed (EBT thrust, power cap, submerged drag)
equations.source: Lighthill 1971 (recalled); muscle power cap is an assumption

equations.label: Taxi
equations.source: quasi-steady feathering foil; Hoerner spray drag (recalled)

parameter_unknowns: Looming threshold, predator speed, size and start distance, and starting depth are assumptions. The capture fraction depends mostly on them.
Muscle mechanical power (50-250 W/kg muscle), the 50% muscle fraction and the 0.75 propulsive efficiency are assumptions. Emergence speed scales with them.
The taxi lobe area, feathering limit (6-15 deg) and residual wetted-hull fraction (0-10%) are assumptions, and they decide whether take-off speed is reached.
Body length 0.171 m comes from an assumed condition factor; the organism glide manifest gives mass only.
open_questions: What emergence speed and angle do free flying fish actually show? This model predicts a few m/s underwater, with the taxi supplying the rest.
Is Edgerton & Breder's 50-70 Hz taxi beat compatible with the muscle twitch limit at sea temperature?
m1-fast-start.perturbation_sweep: Fixed one factor at a time (4,000 draws each, same seed): Mauthner path latency 5-320 ms; muscle corner frequency 20-70 Hz; commanded emergence angle 15-60 deg; muscle power 50-1000 W/kg muscle. Effects on P(caught), P(emerge), P(take-off) and emergence speed and angle are in results.json 'sweep'.
m1-fast-start.experiment_design: Calibrate with (a) synchronised underwater and aerial high-speed video of wild flying-fish launches (emergence speed and path angle, taxi duration and speed history, tail-beat frequency), and (b) looming-stimulus trials on captive juveniles or halfbeaks (latency distribution, escape trajectories, response probability). Falsifier: emergence at 8-10 m/s or more with only a small taxi increment would refute the power-limited chain.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED, not observed. The predator is a pure-pursuit point, not an animal, so capture fractions compare model variants only.
No neuron is simulated. The Mauthner cell is reduced to a threshold plus a latency, and the C-start to a yaw turn plus a speed jump.
Escape kinematics come from goldfish, zebrafish and multi-species reviews; none is fitted to Exocoetidae.
Release at h0 = 0.1 m with gamma0 = 0 is an assumed continuity condition. The h0 = 1 m numbers are only for comparison with the glide-fixed-launch card.

couplings.kind: launch-speed distribution into engineering/simulation/glide.integrate (same organism polar)
thrust, drag and muscle functions imported

m2-caudal-cpg.model_name: behavior-cpg phase/amplitude chain (imported unchanged) + detuning + muscle low-pass + Lighthill EBT thrust + quasi-steady taxi lobe
m2-caudal-cpg.context: Extends behavior-cpg and does not duplicate it: engineering.behavior.model.cpg() and rk4() are imported. Added here: the phase-locking stability of that chain under a descending-drive frequency gradient; the body wavelength set by the chain's phase lag; thrust, drag, power and speed equilibria; and a re-run of behavior-cpg's own servo across its declared 15-45 Hz band.
m2-caudal-cpg.time_units: seconds (CPG integration, dt 0.1 ms); speed equilibria are steady states

equations.label: Reused oscillator chain with added detuning
equations.source: Ijspeert et al. 2007 form, as implemented in engineering/behavior/model.py

equations.label: Locking and stability of the unidirectional chain
equations.source: derived here; checked against numerical integration and a numerical Jacobian

equations.label: Elongated-body thrust
equations.source: Lighthill 1971 (recalled), checked by phase averaging

equations.label: Muscle low-pass (assumed form)
equations.source: assumption; Wardle 1975 motivates the twitch limit

parameter_unknowns: Tail amplitude, caudal span, wavelength, drag augmentation and wetted area are assumptions and are swept.
The muscle corner frequency f_m is a swept assumption; no Exocoetidae muscle data was used.
The taxi lobe model (area, aspect ratio, passive feathering limit) is assumed; no flying-fish caudal-lobe measurement was used.
open_questions: Which kinematic recording of Exocoetidae burst swimming (f, H, lambda against U) would calibrate EBT here?
Does the reticulospinal drive impose a frequency gradient along the body? Locking is lost beyond |(N-1)dw| = c.
m2-caudal-cpg.perturbation_sweep: Terminal speed over tail-beat frequency 4-80 Hz x amplitude 0.05-0.15 L x muscle corner 20-70 Hz x wavelength 0.8-1.2 L x drag factor 1-3 (8,580 equilibria); locking over coupling 10-120 1/s x detuning 0-6 Hz per segment (48 integrations); taxi top speed over power 50-250 W/kg x wetted-hull fraction 0-10%.
m2-caudal-cpg.experiment_design: Measure tail-beat frequency, tail amplitude and body wavelength against speed in burst-swimming and taxiing flying fish (high-speed video), and run work-loop experiments on axial white muscle at habitat temperature (power against cycle frequency). Falsifier: muscle power of about 1000 W/kg or more, or an emergence faster than the power-capped EBT equilibrium.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED, not observed. EBT is an inviscid reactive-force theory; the drag model is a flat-plate estimate.
The CPG is the behavior-cpg phase-oscillator abstraction, not a spinal circuit; phase lag is imposed, not emergent.
Agreement with Bainbridge's empirical speed-frequency relation is a recalled comparison, not a fit or a validation for flying fish.
behavior-cpg's servo is a designed actuator; its tracking results say nothing about fish muscle.

m3-glide-stabilizer.model_name: Linear small-perturbation glider (longitudinal [u, alpha, q, theta]; lateral [beta, p, r, phi]) with delayed vestibular/visual feedback to pelvic and pectoral fins
m3-glide-stabilizer.context: Plant from ff-organ's r3-daane printed glider geometry and trim rule (CG = NP - 8% MAC), plus ff-organ's aeroelastic lift-slope factor. Stability is computed exactly for the delayed linear loop, with one delay chain per sensed channel. Failures come from a Monte Carlo with fin saturation, gusts and sensor noise. Otolith signals are derived from the plant's specific force, so in flight the otolith 'bank' signal reflects sideslip and is not the bank angle.
m3-glide-stabilizer.time_units: seconds of glide (2 ms discrete step)

equations.label: Delayed output feedback
equations.source: design choice; exact discrete delay chains

equations.label: Otolith signals in flight
equations.source: gravito-inertial specific force (standard mechanics)

equations.label: Static margin and neutral point
equations.source: textbook flight mechanics (recalled); repo hand-NP method family

parameter_unknowns: The caudal fin as vertical surface (area fraction 0.05-0.30 of pectoral area, arm 0.06 m) is assumed; the print geometry has no separate caudal surface in flight_model.json.
Fin actuator lag (20 ms), authority (+-15 deg), controller bandwidths and sensor noise are assumptions.
Trim CL 0.6, CD0 0.06 and e 0.8 are design assumptions shared with the organism glide polar.
open_questions: What are fin-muscle EMG latencies after an imposed pitch or roll in flying fish?
Do flying fish use vision for bank in flight? Test with vision occluded in a tethered or wind-tunnel preparation.
m3-glide-stabilizer.perturbation_sweep: Exact closed-loop spectral radius over canal delay 0-100 ms x vision delay 0-200 ms, over gain 0.1-10 x nominal, over static margin -10 to 30% MAC, and over dihedral 0-14 deg x vertical-surface fraction 0.05-0.30 at 25 g and 50 g. Failure Monte Carlo over gust 0.25-2 m/s x vision delay 30-150 ms for vision, otolith, rate-only and passive configurations.
m3-glide-stabilizer.experiment_design: Fly an IMU-instrumented r3-daane print through measured gusts to check the linear plant and its modes. In animals: imposed-perturbation trials (tethered or wind tunnel) with and without vision, recording fin EMG latency and attitude recovery. Falsifier: robust bank recovery with vision blocked in a coordinated glide would reveal a non-visual bank cue that this model lacks.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED, not observed. A stabilising PD loop shows that some controller with these delays could work, not that fish use it.
Linear, quasi-steady aerodynamics with no ground effect (which Park & Choi 2010 show matters near the surface), no unsteady flow and no fin twist.
The 50 g case assumes the same geometry, CG and radii of gyration as the 25 g print.
Vestibular and visual systems are reduced to delays plus white noise; canal high-pass dynamics and visual processing are not modelled.

couplings.kind: trim rule SM 8% MAC and r3-daane geometry

j1-m1-sobol.model_name: Saltelli/Sobol global sensitivity of M1 (32 inputs: 26 priors + 6 internal draws; first-order and total indices with bootstrap intervals)
j1-m1-sobol.context: It answers which unknowns would most change M1's predictions if measured. It ran as Nebius CPU job claude-neuro-j1-m1-sobol-a1: 139,264 model runs in each of two scenarios, one with the predator and one kinematic-only with the predator disabled.
j1-m1-sobol.time_units: none: variance decomposition over the prior box

equations.label: Total index (Jansen)
equations.source: Jansen 1999 form; Saltelli 2010 first-order form

parameter_unknowns: The indices are relative to the uniform prior boxes in fast_start.PRIORS; narrower or wider boxes change the ranking.
open_questions: Can axial white-muscle power and taxi wetted drag be measured in Exocoetidae? Together they control take-off in this model.
j1-m1-sobol.perturbation_sweep: Every input varies jointly over its prior box (scrambled Sobol design, N 4096, d 32). The inert inputs in the kinematic scenario serve as a built-in null.
j1-m1-sobol.experiment_design: Measure first what has the largest total index. For take-off: muscle power (in-situ work loops at habitat temperature), taxi wetted fraction and taxi duration (high-speed video of the hull's water contact). For emergence speed: muscle power and the swimming drag factor (PIV, or deceleration during glides between beats). For capture: predator approach speed (field video). Mauthner latency explains almost none of the variance within 5-20 ms.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED: these indices rank the model's own priors; they are not measurements and do not show which biology matters in real fish.
A model-form error, such as the EBT thrust law or the taxi lobe model, does not appear in these indices.
Take-off is rare (3.4%) and interaction-dominated (sum of S1 = 0.25), so the first-order indices understate the combined effects.

couplings.kind: global sensitivity of that model (same code; default path reproduced within 1e-9 on the cloud CPU)

j2-m3-atlas.model_name: M3 plant and controller over 112 lateral and 20 longitudinal r3-daane variants: nonlinear-saturation Monte Carlo (GPU) plus exact linear delayed stability (CPU pool)
j2-m3-atlas.context: It maps where a delayed vestibular/visual controller acting through the pectoral and pelvic fins keeps the glider within attitude limits. Axes: caudal-fin area, dihedral, mass, static margin, canal and vision delays, sensor set and gust level. It ran as Nebius H100 job claude-neuro-j2-m3-atlas-a2; the first attempt's output was lost in transport and no result is claimed from it.
j2-m3-atlas.time_units: 5 s of glide per trajectory, 2 ms step

equations.label: Failure probability
equations.source: failure rule as in M3

parameter_unknowns: The caudal-fin vertical-surface fraction and arm, fin lag and authority, and noise levels are assumptions; the plant is linear and quasi-steady.
open_questions: Which caudal-fin area and dihedral does the printed r3-daane actually have, measured as a vertical-surface fraction?
j2-m3-atlas.perturbation_sweep: Full factorial: lateral 2 masses x 8 dihedrals x 7 k_v; longitudinal 2 masses x 10 static margins; MC delays canal 0-80 ms x vision 0-200 ms; sensor sets vision/otolith/rate-only/passive; gust 0.5/1/2 m/s; 2048 trajectories per cell. Linear atlas: canal 0-100 ms x vision 0-200 ms x gain 0.3/1/3.
j2-m3-atlas.experiment_design: Fly instrumented prints with two or three caudal-fin areas and dihedrals chosen from the atlas's boundary cells, under measured gusts, and compare the observed upset rates with these predictions. In animals, measure the fin EMG latency after an imposed roll to place a fish on the delay axis.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED, not observed: a linear quasi-steady plant with assumed fin authority and lag; no unsteady aerodynamics or ground effect.
The Monte Carlo applies the same-step actuator state, one step (2 ms) less lag than the linear atlas (see integration_note).
A stable controller shows feasibility, not what fish do.

j3-m5-mcell.model_name: Leaky integrate-and-fire Mauthner cell with feedforward inhibition, driven by three candidate looming encoders (Preuss kappa, LGMD eta, pure angle)
j3-m5-mcell.context: This is the first simulated neuron in the project. It asks which encoding reproduces measured looming-escape signatures, using criteria preregistered in the code before the run. The response angles and latencies of the consistent sets are candidates to replace M1's assumed threshold and latency priors. It ran as Nebius H100 job claude-neuro-j3-m5-mcell-a2.
j3-m5-mcell.time_units: seconds of stimulus (0.5 ms step) from looming onset at 5 deg

equations.label: M-cell
equations.source: reduced LIF with feedforward inhibition (assumption)

equations.label: Encoders
equations.tex: d_\kappa=\theta e^{-\beta\theta},\ d_\eta=\dot\theta e^{-\beta\theta},\ d_\theta=\theta\ (\text{delayed by }\delta)
equations.source: Preuss 2006; Hatsopoulos 1995 / Gabbiani 2002

parameter_unknowns: All neuron parameters (delay, gains, time constants, noise) are swept assumptions; no fish electrophysiology is fitted.
open_questions: Do flying fish escape at a fixed looming angle (as larval zebrafish do), and at what angle?
All three encoders pass the abstract-level criteria at similar rates (1-1.6% of parameter space), so these criteria cannot discriminate them; per-l/v response-angle data would.
j3-m5-mcell.perturbation_sweep: 8 neuron parameters x 3 encoders (16,384 scrambled-Sobol sets each) x 7 approach parameters l/v 10-240 ms x 32 noisy trials.
j3-m5-mcell.experiment_design: Present looming disks with l/v 10-240 ms to captive flying-fish juveniles or halfbeaks, with high-speed video. Measure the response angle and latency for each l/v: a fixed-angle threshold separates the theta/kappa-like encoders from eta. Pharmacological reduction of inhibition (glycine/GABA antagonists, as in the M-cell literature) tests the role of the feedforward-inhibition parameter.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED: a single reduced neuron, not the tectum-to-M-cell circuit.
Criteria come from abstracts of goldfish (Preuss 2006) and larval zebrafish (Bhattacharyya 2017; Temizer 2015) studies, not flying fish.
Passing the criteria shows consistency only; it does not identify a mechanism.
The lower tail of the consistent response angles (5.5-6 deg) sits near the 5 deg stimulus onset: a floor set by the stimulus protocol, not a measured threshold.

couplings.kind: candidate replacement for the theta_thr and latency priors

j4-m3-sobol.model_name: Saltelli/Sobol global sensitivity of the M3 lateral loop over 14 design, neural, fin-muscle and environment inputs
j4-m3-sobol.context: It answers which parameter, measured or redesigned, most changes the glider's chance of staying upright. Outputs: Monte Carlo failure probability (128 trajectories per point), exact linear instability and log spectral radius. It ran as Nebius H100 job claude-neuro-j4-m3-sobol-a1.
j4-m3-sobol.time_units: none: variance decomposition (each point is a 5 s Monte Carlo)

equations.label: Total index (Jansen)
equations.source: as in J1

parameter_unknowns: The indices depend on the declared input boxes (sobol_m3.IN).
open_questions: Is the decisive parameter a design choice (caudal area, dihedral) or a neural one (delays, gains)? See the indices.
j4-m3-sobol.perturbation_sweep: All 14 inputs vary jointly: N 2048, 32,768 points, 4.2M trajectories.
j4-m3-sobol.experiment_design: Prioritise measurements by total index: geometry (caudal vertical-surface area, dihedral) from the specimen or print; neural delays from fin EMG latency after imposed roll; fin actuator lag and authority from muscle twitch kinetics and range of motion.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED: ranks the model's priors; linear quasi-steady plant.
Monte Carlo noise is part of the failure variance; its share is reported.
Compute note: the 4.2M-trajectory Monte Carlo took 15 s on the H100; the job did not strictly need a GPU.

j6-m5-design.model_name: Experiment design for M5: candidate looming protocols x the J3-consistent parameter sets of each encoder; nearest-centroid discrimination vs number of fish
j6-m5-design.context: It sizes the experiment that would tell kappa, eta and pure-angle encoding apart, which J3's abstract-level criteria could not do. It ran as Nebius H100 job claude-neuro-j6-m5-design-a1.
j6-m5-design.time_units: seconds of stimulus from looming onset (0.5 ms step)

equations.label: Classifier
equations.source: nearest standardised centroid (design choice)

parameter_unknowns: The candidate fish are drawn from J3's consistent sets; real between-fish variability is unknown.
open_questions: Is the 2 deg onset feasible on a real display at the fish's viewing distance?
j6-m5-design.perturbation_sweep: 3 protocols (J3's; 2 deg onset; 2 deg onset with l/v 5-500 ms) x 3 encoders x consistent sets x 64 trials; accuracy for 1-32 fish.
j6-m5-design.experiment_design: Result: the J3-like protocol (5 deg onset, l/v 10-240 ms) discriminates the three encoder hypotheses best, at 81% accuracy with 8 fish and 89% with 16 (chance 33%). The 2 deg onset and wide 5-500 ms protocols did worse (72% and 70% with 8 fish). Plan: at least 16 fish per hypothesis, a looming-disk series at l/v 10-240 ms, response angle and latency per trial.
does_not_establish: SIMULATED sizing: assumes the real encoder is one of the three model forms, and that fish vary like the consistent parameter sets.
Selection bias: the consistent sets were selected under the J3 protocol, so they cluster most tightly there; the advantage of that protocol may be partly an artefact of that selection.

j7-m3-atlas-refined.context: A print-tolerance band for ff-organ around J2's recommendation. It ran as Nebius H100 job claude-neuro-j7-m3-atlas-refined-a1 with 4096 trajectories per cell.

j7-m3-atlas-refined.experiment_design: Result for the print: dihedral 0-2 deg gives ~0% roll upset even at 3 m/s gusts for k_v >= 0.125; 3-4 deg is ~0% at 2 m/s but 16-29% at 3 m/s; 7 deg is 41-49% at 2 m/s. Between k_v 0.10 (always fails) and 0.125 (fine) the response is a cliff, so print at k_v >= 0.15 for margin. Mass 25-35 g barely matters. Test by flying 0, 2 and 4 deg prints under measured gusts (print_band_tables.json).
